transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, what brings me in is that I've just gotten so... slowed down lately. Like, I can sit there staring at one audit workpaper for twenty minutes before I even move my hand to type. It's just... I don't know, it's taking me forever to do anything, and people at work have really started noticing that I'm not keeping up.
Have you ever experienced a period of time where you felt unusually energetic, talkative, or impulsive, to the point where others might have noticed you were acting differently than your usual self?

No, I don't think so. I've never really had a time where I was super energetic or... impulsive. I'm usually pretty steady. Or at least I was, before I got so bogged down. But no, I haven't experienced anything like what you're describing.
Have you ever experienced a similar period of feeling this slowed down or low in the past, or is this the first time you've ever felt this way?

No, this is... this is really the first time. I mean, I've been tired before, especially during busy season at work, but never anything like this. I've never felt this low or just... completely unable to get my brain to move. So, yeah, it's definitely a first for me.
Have you noticed any new physical symptoms, such as headaches, vision changes, or unexplained changes in your coordination or memory, since this started?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. No headaches or vision problems. And my coordination seems fine, I guess. It's really just the... the slowness and feeling so low. But physically, like you're asking, no, nothing new.
Are you currently taking any new medications, supplements, or have you recently had any major changes to your medical health or chronic conditions?

No, I haven't started anything new. No new medications or... supplements, or anything like that. And my health has been pretty normal otherwise. I don't really have any chronic conditions, so there haven't been any major changes there either.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or the amount of food you've been eating since you started feeling this way?

Yeah, my appetite has definitely changed. I just... I don't really want to eat. Food has mostly become something I just force down because I know I should. And I've noticed my work skirts have gotten loose lately, even though I'm definitely not trying to lose weight. So, yeah, I guess I am eating a lot less.
Are you able to perform your basic daily tasks, like showering, dressing, or getting out of bed, or have you become completely unable to care for yourself?

I can still get out of bed and shower, usually, though it's... it's a lot harder than it used to be. But the bigger problem is keeping up with my actual responsibilities. At work, I've missed review deadlines, and I've actually had to hand off parts of audits that I normally manage all by myself. And at home, it's the same. My husband has had to take over paying the bills and dealing with insurance forms because I just... I can't reliably get through them right now.
Are you able to experience any pleasure or interest in the hobbies or activities that you used to enjoy, or has that feeling of 'slowness' affected those things too?

No, I really don't enjoy much of anything lately. I used to be pretty active... I'd plan weekend hikes, take a lot of photos, and I always used to spend Sundays cooking. I even volunteered at the local library. But now... I don't know, those things just feel like items on a checklist that I don't even care enough to start. I just don't have any interest in them anymore.

When you are sitting there staring at your work, have people around you noticed that you are physically moving much slower than usual, or perhaps that your speech has become noticeably slower or quieter?

Yeah, they have. Actually, that's a big part of what brings me in. I've just gotten so... slowed down lately. I can sit there staring at one audit workpaper for twenty minutes before I even move my hand to type. It's like I'm just stuck. So, yeah, people at work have definitely started noticing that I'm not keeping up.
